structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineItem` are the prescribed type and signatures. Both roots implement them.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#struct[OutlineItem]` has `#[non_exhaustive]`. Its public fields are `selector`, `kind`, `span`, `name_span: Option<Span>`, `header_span`, `trailer_span`, `structural_hash` and `attachments: Vec<OutlineAttachment>`. It also has a private `own_hash` field, which matches the text's "/* private fields */". It derives `Clone` and `Debug`, as the trait implementations in the text require. Changing any field name or type, dropping `non_exhaustive`, or removing a derive would break the prescribed declaration while behaving the same at runtime.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineItem]` declares `new(selector, kind, span, structural_hash)`. It initializes `name_span`, `header_span` and `trailer_span` to `None`, `own_hash` to `None` and `attachments` to an empty `Vec`. It declares `with_name_span`, `with_header_span`, `with_trailer_span` and `with_own_hash`, each taking `self` and returning `Self`. `with_attachments` sets the list to the supplied `Vec`. These signatures and initial values match the text.

The prose also describes `span`, `name_span` and `attachments` semantics. Those clauses are delegated to the cited `Span`, `name_span` and `attachments` requirements, which are assessed on their own text. The `with_own_hash` clause ("A language supplies the digest excluding descendants … when it differs") is behavioral and sets the private `own_hash`. The remaining clauses specify only observable behavior and need no extra implementation roots.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each behavioral obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineItem`.

- **Constructor defaults:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` calls `OutlineItem::new`. It asserts `name_span == None`, `header_span` and `trailer_span` are `None`, and `attachments` is empty. This covers the `new` initialization obligations.
- **Builders and field preservation:** The same test applies `with_header_span`, `with_trailer_span` and `with_name_span`. It then clones the outline and asserts `selector`, `kind`, `span`, `structural_hash`, `name_span`, `header_span` and `trailer_span` all keep their values.
- **Attachments:** The test calls `with_attachments` twice. It asserts only the second list (a single `Annotation` attachment with span 4..6) remains, so the call sets the list and does not append.
- **Clone and Debug:** The test clones the `Outline` and its items, and formats it with `{:?}`. The Debug check only asserts non-empty output, but the requirement states no specific Debug format.
- **`with_own_hash`:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` uses `CustomLanguage::outline`, which sets the root's own hash through `with_own_hash`. The root's `structural_hash()` is `"a hello z"`. Its fingerprint value is `"a  z"` with scheme `custom-v2:own-v1`, so the supplied own digest, which differs from the structural hash, is what gets used. The test also checks that selecting `part[selected]` keeps `structural_hash` `"selected-digest"`.
- **Struct shape and `#[non_exhaustive]`:** These are structural obligations. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the public export inventory against rustdoc and compiles the Habeas consumer against the SDK.
- **Cited requirements:** `requirements.sdk.outlines.Span`, `requirements.sdk.outlines.name_span` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments` are cited context. Their obligations are not reassessed here.

pub fn with_name_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_header_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_trailer_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_own_hash(self, hash: String) -> Self;
pub fn with_attachments(self, attachments: Vec<OutlineAttachment>) -> Self;
`trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
A named item's `name_span` is `Some` with the span to highlight for its name
in the original source snapshot. The highlighted text may differ from the
name in the selector. Use `selector` to address the item. The file root and
anonymous items have `name_span` set to `None`. `OutlineItem::new` starts with
`None`. Language providers use `with_name_span` to set the highlight within

An *attachment* is a source construct that an outline language associates
with an outline item. A documentation comment on a Rust function and a
decorator on a Python method are examples.
